# Skill: route

# Route

This file is the process. It is the same in every project and on every machine. The job table is `skills/ROUTE.md` in the repo you are in. That table is the only project-specific part.

Search the table. Do not read it end to end. Take one row.

1. A cell that starts with `node ` is the command. Run it. Open nothing else.
2. A cell that says `none` is a Make. Open the one file that row names.
3. Two When cells still match. Stop and ask. Do not open both.

A task the table does not name is still this process. In the same commit, add one row: when it applies, which file to open, which files to leave closed. A second task that hits the same row replaces the sentence that failed, or adds one trap sentence when that row has none for this miss. The same trap on two rows moves into `skills/shared/<name>.md`, and the rows keep that name. A trap is the command or the refusal. It does not cite an archive.

A better way replaces the old one in the same edit. Delete the sentence, the step, or the row it retires. Add with nothing deleted only when the table had no row. The route changes when When, Open, or Leave closed changed. The how-to changes in the one file that row already opens, and it is not copied into a second skill or an archive. A trap that was already written, and the miss still shipped, is replaced by the check. It is not given another sentence. One miss replaces one instruction. A rejected method is one line, or it is gone. The attempt stays in git.

A script becomes a command cell only when it imports the parts it reuses. A script that draws those parts stays `none`.

A run that followed a `node` cell and matched edits neither the table nor an archive.

Paths are relative to the repo root. Nothing in this process uses a home directory, a machine name, or a secret. A commit of `skills/route/`, `skills/ROUTE.md`, `skills/shared/`, and `tooling/check-route.js` is the copy the next laptop, desktop, or VM gets with `git pull`.

## Another project

Copy `skills/route/` and `tooling/check-route.js`. Copy `skills/route/TEMPLATE.md` to `skills/ROUTE.md` and fill the rows for that project. Add a file under `skills/shared/` only when a row names it. Generate `tooling/route-grandfather.json` from the folders that already exist, then wire `node tooling/check-route.js` into that project's check. Do not copy another project's component table.

<skill_content name="figma-uikit-to-design">
# Skill: figma-uikit-to-design

# UI kit → design file (live rebuild)

`use_figma` runs inside ONE file per call and the Plugin API has no
cross-file node clone. So: **extract everything in the source, recreate with
live imports in the target.** Do not export SVG and re-import it — that
flattens instances, variables, and auto-layout bindings.

Requires: a write-capable MCP connection (see `figma-mcp-connect`), edit
access to the target, and the target subscribed to the same libraries.
Load official `figma-use` (+ `figma-generate-design` for screens) first.

## 0. Look the part up before you draw it

A part the library publishes is an INSTANCE, never a drawing - and the lookup is
a file in the repo, not an inference. On 2026-10-15 four stripes on the Sage 50 CA
page were rebuilt because they had drawn what already existed: slider arrows as
cards with an ASCII `<` ("the live chevron is a private-use glyph, unavailable in
Figma") when the library publishes `Control: slider arrows` at exactly the live
32x32; slider dots as hand-drawn ovals where `Control: indicator` exists; an
accordion row with no chevron at all where `Accordion panels` carries a
`chevron_down`; and three stripes whose repeating items were re-created as frames
instead of instancing the kit's `Highlight` + its `Image for icons` slot.

```sh
node tooling/kit-inventory.js --find 'slider arrow|accordion|indicator|badge'
node tooling/kit-inventory.js --write     # refresh docs/kit-components.md + .json
grep -i 'accordion' docs/kit-components.md   # same thing, offline
```

- **`Sage.com UI library v3.0`** (`gRSlZwfShMFfzCyrDUfSGd`, 627 components)
  holds the parts: `Highlight`, `Section hero`, `Button`, `Image for icons`,
  `Accordion panels`, `Control: slider arrows`, `Control: indicator`,
  `Footer`, `Main navigation`, tokens. `docs/kit-components.md` lists every one
  with its set, key and node id; `GET /v1/files/<file>/nodes?ids=<node id>&depth=9`
  prints a master's whole construction (this is how "`Accordion panels` IS a text
  plus `chevron_down`" was established).
- **Icon masters** come from a different library (`WBrrBwoeb7reGSVmxGw1YJ`, pages
  `Spot icons` / `Detailed icons`, variant axes `Colour`/`State`/`Size`). They are
  not in the kit cache: record every icon key in the consuming section's `spec.json`
  (`spotIcons` / `iconMasters`) with the live artwork it matches, or say that no
  artwork exists and the master was chosen by meaning.
- **The kit's own pattern frames** (e.g. `LC01 - Desktop`) live in a third file
  that a REST token may not be able to read; read them with the plugin while that
  file is open, or read the components the frame instances.
- **Write it as the engine's part types** (`figma/lib/stripe.js`): `instance`
  (a part by key, with `props`/`hides`/`texts`/`at`), `icon` (the pattern's own
  `Image for icons` slot with a master swapped in), `highlight` (the kit's
  repeating item, copy written into the kit's own text nodes) - and add
  `kit: {set, variant, key}` so the build ASSERTS the node is that component
  (`PASS slider prev IS the kit component "Control: slider arrows"`). A text
  inside an instance can be re-bound: `texts: [{node, copy, sizeVar, fillVar}]`.
- **When the library really has nothing** (CN05's Canadian strap badge: live art is
  an inline SVG the library does not carry), write `kitGap: "<why>"` where the node
  is drawn. The gate then reports the reason instead of failing, and a ruling is
  distinguishable from an oversight.
- **The gate**: `node tooling/check-kit-parts.js --selftest` proves the rules; the
  gate itself fails an ASCII-as-icon, a raster-as-icon, a chrome role with no
  kit backing, a component key that is in neither the cache nor that section's
  prose, and icons with no recorded provenance.

## 1. Locate the source frame (pages load lazily)

With `documentAccess: dynamic-page`, touching `page.children` throws until
loaded. Always load first, then search:

```js
for (const page of figma.root.children){ await page.loadAsync(); }
const node = figma.root.findOne(function(x){ return x.id === '64:64227'; });
```

## 2. Dump geometry + layout skeleton

Record per node: type, name, x/y/w/h, `layoutMode`, `itemSpacing`,
paddings, sizing modes. `get_metadata` on the frame is the cheap version;
a walk script gives the full tree. Keep ASCII-only code (exotic characters
have caused spurious `SyntaxError`s through some transports).

## 3. Dump instances: keys, props, texts (the critical call)

One walk returning `{path, name, mainComponent{name,key}, componentProperties, text}`.
Paginate if the return nears ~20KB:

```js
function walk(n, path){
  // INSTANCE → {name, mc:{name,key}, props:{k:{t:type,v:value}}}
  // TEXT → {name, text: characters.slice(0,300)}
  // recurse children with path + '/' + i
}
```

What this reveals (real PN08 case): nested `Highlight`/`Section hero`/
`RTE`/`Paragraph`/icon instances are **remote** (`importComponentByKeyAsync`
targets), variant props are plain names (`style`, `Colour`, `Size`,
`has theme dark`), and icon slots differ per card (`accountant support`,
`awards`, `automation`).

## 4. Recreate in the target with live imports

```js
const results = await Promise.all([
  figma.importComponentByKeyAsync(HERO_KEY),
  figma.importComponentByKeyAsync(HL_KEY),
  figma.importComponentByKeyAsync(ICON_KEYS[0]), // ...
]);
// skeleton frames FIRST (createAutoLayout, resize, center), then:
const inst = comp.createInstance();
parent.appendChild(inst);
inst.resize(W, H);
```

Rules that bite: never assign `figma.currentPage =` (use
`await figma.setCurrentPageAsync()`); `resize()` resets sizing modes to
FIXED — call it before setting HUG/FILL, or set FIXED explicitly after
appending to auto-layout parents; load EVERY font style before touching
`characters` (the missing one surfaces as `Cannot write to node with
unloaded font "X Y"` — commonly the Bold style).

## 5. Apply overrides: props, icon swaps, texts

- Variants: `inst.setProperties({style:'single cta'})` (plain names work).
- **Nested icon swaps: `instance.swapComponent(comp)` EXISTS and works.**
  Find the slot icon inside the imported instance, swap to the source's
  icon key, rename to match (`slotIcon.name = 'awards'`).
- Texts: unmanaged TEXT nodes accept direct `characters` writes (fonts
  loaded); TEXT-type component properties go through `setProperties`.
- Return all created node IDs from every call (no state persists across calls).

## 6. Theme variables (or dark mode silently breaks)

Hardcoded fills don't follow modes. Mirror the source bindings:

```js
// source probe: node.boundVariables.fills → getVariableByIdAsync → {key,name}
const v = await figma.variables.importVariableByKeyAsync(VAR_KEY);
const bound = figma.variables.setBoundVariableForPaint(
  {type:'SOLID', color:{r:1,g:1,b:1}}, 'color', v);
node.fills = [bound];   // setBoundVariableForPaint returns a NEW paint
```

Test both modes without asking the user: resolve the collection's
`over dark` / `over light` modeIds and
`frame.setExplicitVariableModeForCollection(coll, modeId)`, screenshot each,
leave the file on light. Wrapper frames the generator creates default to
white fills — clear to transparent (`fills = []`) if the source wrappers are.
Section backgrounds get an explicit bound paint, not a mirror (mirrors rot
when the source node is deleted — learning 82):

```js
// bg variable resolved once by KEY (boundVariables.fills → getVariableByIdAsync)
const bgv = await figma.variables.importVariableByKeyAsync(BG_KEY);
frame.fills = [figma.variables.setBoundVariableForPaint(
  {type:'SOLID', color:{r:0,g:0,b:0}}, 'color', bgv)];
```

Notes from the PN02 rebuild: there is NO node-level mode getter (only the
setter); modes may be per-section, not page-wide — never assume inherited
context. `layoutAlign` on nested instance children is a silent no-op
(center via the parent frame's `counterAxisAlignItems`); nested-frame
`resize()` likewise. Full catalog: `skills/figma-component-edit` §4.

## 7. Verify visually, iterate

Screenshot source frame AND target frame at the same size; compare side by
side; fix discrepancies; repeat. Checks: icon identity per card, text
content, alignment/centering, both theme modes.

## Known fidelity limits (say these upfront)

- The current library may have **drifted** from the source file's version
  (e.g. Section hero gained icon+subtitle rows) — instancing then ADDS
  elements the original lacks. Fallback: static centered text for that part.
- Unbound source text (e.g. a title with plain fill) stays unbound in the
  rebuild — parity, not improvement.
- `use_figma` code has a ~50KB limit and returns ~20KB — split extract/build
  across calls. The CA page's engine now sends the comment-stripped payload and
  keeps the commented copy in the temp file it prints, which is worth ~7.5KB.
- "The library has no such icon" is a hypothesis, not a fact: check
  `docs/kit-components.md` (and for icons, resolve the candidate key over REST)
  before drawing a glyph, and record the key you used. `docs/kit-components.md`
  says what exists; `tooling/check-kit-parts.js` is what stops the next agent
  from re-learning it.
